title: Radio, 08:25: Riverside Sweep at 412 of 680, Vault Breaker Deadline

fields.centerName: Emergency Operations Center, Campus Services Building Room 108

lines.text: EOC, Riverside. My RAs started knocking on their floors at 07:50 on their own, because residents were already in the halls, whether or not anyone has told me to go. Floors 1 through 5 report clear. 6 through 11 are still knocking, and the stair tower is slow. Both oxygen residents are on 9 with the nurse, waiting for the elevator. One RA can't tell me whether anyone has knocked for our deaf resident.

My roster says 680. The RA floor sheets add up to 412 out so far, and I can't match names to the sheets. Some residents are walking to 08:00 classes across the Lower Quad, and the paths are awash. I need two answers from you right now. Is this an evacuation order with Kessler as the destination? And who tells me when to give up the elevator?
EOC, Kessler registration, status. Kessler Fieldhouse is open. Registered, three one eight. Cots set, six hundred. Generator outlets are low, two reserved for oxygen. Water is okay.

Ops, Electrician 1 in the Riverside vault. There's water seeping into the vault sump. I can hold the main breaker closed until about 09:15, no later. After that I'm pulling it whether the elevators are empty or not, or I'm getting out of here.

fields.voiceStyle: Riverside: woman in her forties, controlled but strained, slightly breathless from stairs. Kessler: young male student worker, flat and quick, reading numbers. Electrician: older male, blunt, tense, echo of a concrete room.

instructorNote: This is the main Riverside decision point. The IC should now order the evacuation, or confirm an order already given, by naming the area, the clearance time and Kessler, and log the 0720 AM crest of 10.8 ft as the basis. The IC should also move residents off the Lower Quad. Watch whether DoS sends someone to knock for the deaf resident, holds an elevator on 9 for the oxygen residents and treats the 268 unmatched names (680 minus 412) as unaccounted for. Kessler's 318 registered does not match the 412 out, which is a second gap to reconcile. Fac should keep the breaker closed until the IC confirms the elevators are clear and before the 09:15 limit. Hand the TA's written note to the Student Evaluators at the same time. It tells them to timestamp the Riverside order, the first MSU Alert, the correction to the roof rumor and the breaker opening, and to note any confirmation the seats exchange before it.
